parsed.explanation: For an adult travelling alone, the sharpest risk is border/airport screening: passport/visa marker rules can force disclosure, refusal, stranding or referral to federal custody with reported abuse; federal government-funded single-sex facility restrictions remain universal. For an adult travelling with a minor, local shield law, school protections and public-accommodation law reduce care and facility risk in the division, but federal anti-minor-care orders and subpoena/funding threats create uncertain preemption exposure. The combined score reflects high severity at federal stages partly offset by operative local protections, yielding Elevated Risk rather than Reduced or High.

entry_documents.exposure: Documented. Passports/visas require binary birth-sex marker; mismatches trigger refusal, additional evidence and possible permanent fraud ineligibility; reports of confiscated/blocked passports and stranded travellers; existing X still valid but not protected in this division.
entry_documents.protection: Not documented. Division law does not control passports, visas, ports of entry; local X/state IDs do not offset federal document screening.
entry_documents.interaction: Border stage is federal. It occurs before division protections can apply; refusal or fraud finding creates departure/stranding or referral to immigration custody.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented severe harm if detained: immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse; corrections policies remove hormones/force conversion therapy; data on transgender prisoners stopped.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented as operative for visitors. National courts and injunctions contest orders but do not show release, consular access, or immunity in custody.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A document mismatch or fraud suspicion can escalate entry review into immigration detention where local public accommodations and shield laws cannot prevent federal custody.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Documented federal order bars government-funded single-sex facilities matching identity; airport screening guide warns pat-downs; many parent states criminalise or ban facilities. Federal spaces remain restricted even in division.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Documented locally: public-accommodation and gender-neutral restroom rules, largest-city all-gender schools, no local bathroom ban; but local law is not shown to pre-empt or nullify federal facilities.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Exposure varies by funding/ownership; non-federal local spaces safer, federal buildings, ports, transit security and federally funded sites carry birth-sex restriction.

care_services.exposure: Documented federal hostility to trans care, minors-care bans, funding threats, hospital subpoenas and reimbursement proposals; local federal funding rules may still bite.
care_services.protection: Documented division shield law protects care within it, including patients/providers travelling from banned jurisdictions, and conversion-therapy ban; local clinics/hospitals are likely safer if shield applies.
care_services.interaction: Care in division can be protected locally, but federal investigators/subpoenas may reach providers/records; shield strength against federal action is not documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Documented state threat framing: binary-sex order, removal of pronoun policies, military ban, counterterrorism prioritises radical pro-transgender groups, and support for assigned-sex documents among public.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Documented local protections: gender-identity hate-crime penalties, anti-discrimination law since 2006, panic-defence repeal; national hate-crime statute exists. These protect against local bias but not federal identity law.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Federal framing raises risk at checkpoints/federal venues; division enforcement treats gender identity as protected in local public/private services, reducing street-level hostility if local actors comply.

minors_guardians.exposure: Documented federal executive orders attack minors care/social transition, threaten prosecution of teachers using chosen names/pronouns and funding; polls support sports/binary records; guardian may be investigated only if federal rules reach schools.
minors_guardians.protection: Documented local shield law covers minors travelling for care; school bullying/privacy rules, all-gender bathrooms in largest city, public-accommodation law. Conversion-therapy ban supports youth.
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent bringing a minor for care or schooling encounters federal hostile law at document/border/funding stages but local protective law for care and facilities; federal preemption/subpoena risk uncertain.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No documented visitor-specific anti-trans violence or police targeting in this division; federal document checks can still out travellers. General polls show social pressure, not incident counts.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Documented local anti-discrimination, hate-crime penalties and city/school ordinances likely prompt police response in local venues; national hate-crime law covers gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Street exposure lower in division non-federal venues, but airports, federal buildings and immigration custody remain where national policy overrides local policing.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Documented weak remedy at federal document stage: Supreme Court allowed passport restrictions, suit pending, foreign advisories, no reporting of immigration/transgender custody counts; shield law durability not sourced.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Documented division equality law, complaints/ordinances, legal-aid FAQ, advocacy and courts contesting orders; local non-federal remedies likely work for public accommodation/care claims.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies diverge by actor: local venues and care seekers have operative protection; border, federal facilities, custody and federal school investigations are unremedied or pending.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar border/document exposure: state gender examination, registry, travel denial. Here federal visa screening and fraud permanent ineligibility are comparable, but local shield/public-accommodation protections reduce non-federal facility and care exposure; immigration-custody abuse makes severe stages worse.

Comparable registration/database exposure. Parent passport/visa screening plus federal facilities is harsher, but division public-accommodation law, gender-neutral single-occupancy restrooms and care shield protect local daily life and travelling families, placing combined regime slightly above pure 0.45 registration risk.

Local health/public accommodation protections are stronger than 0.55-C ward mismatch with advocate remedies. But entry screening can refuse/fraud and immigration custody abuse lacks reliable remedy; that unremedied federal tier1 exposure keeps score below 0.55-C.

0.75-C has trained border officers, appeals, compensation. This jurisdiction has hostile federal passport/visa rules and documented custody abuse; protective local layer cannot cancel those. Score sits materially below 0.75-C despite local equality law.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime is split by sovereign level. Entry and federal stages are tier-one exposure: binary passport/visa rules, document discrepancy investigations, possible permanent fraud ineligibility, government-funded facility restrictions, and documented severe immigration/corrections custody harm. These are not neutralised by the division. Within the division, strong public-accommodation law, gender-neutral single-occupancy restrooms, city school policies, hate-crime penalties and a shield law materially lower everyday and minor-care risk, especially for families travelling locally for lawful care. The result is Elevated Risk: safer than a wholly hostile national profile once inside non-federal settings, but still unremedied federal document/custody/facility exposure at the worst stages.
